title: New logo, clearer text, and Chrome folders kept
notes: New ElevenTabs logo: a bookmark with a tick over stacked tabs.
Easier to read everywhere: all small monospace labels are now clear Satoshi type, text is larger, and grey text is darker (or lighter in dark mode).
Import from Chrome now keeps your Chrome folders as folders here, and gives any site with 3 or more bookmarks its own folder. 'Sort unsorted' does the same for what is already imported.
Importing now also turns on Auto-add, so new Chrome bookmarks appear here by themselves.

title: Bookmarks first: folders, right-click and a new dashboard layout
notes: The toolbar popup now opens on Bookmark. Pick a folder, or make a new one right there, and press Save bookmark. A green tick shows on the icon when a page is already bookmarked.
Right-click any page or link, then Bookmark in ElevenTabs, and choose the folder from the menu. Shortcut: Alt+Shift+B.
Dashboard rebuilt with a top bar instead of the sidebar. Bookmarks is the home page, with a paste-a-link bar, a Folders list, and bookmarks grouped by folder.
Folders replace 'categories' everywhere in Bookmarks. Drag a bookmark onto a folder to move it.
Website images fixed (they were stretched).
New permission: contextMenus (for the right-click menu). It shows no warning.

title: A new look, and every bookmark in one sorted place
notes: New Iris design: lighter, cleaner, with a floating sidebar, bolder type and a fresh default theme (Iris, plus Iris Night for dark mode). Your other 9 themes are still there.
Saved is now the home of the dashboard: stats, a By category view with one section per category, favourites on top, and grid or list views.
Bring in all your Chrome bookmarks with one click (copies only). Turn on Auto-add and every bookmark you make in Chrome from then on appears in Saved, in the right category.
Popup and Welcome back page refreshed to match.
If you were on the old Eleven Gold look, you are moved to Iris once. Pick Gold again any time in Appearance.

title: Saved: your own categorised bookmarks, and a new popup
notes: New Saved library: save any page from the popup in one click. It picks a category for you (Dev, AI, Jobs, Shopping and more) and you can change it, add a note or star it.
Library page in the dashboard: search, grid or list view, favourites, bulk move and delete, drag a card onto a category to re-file it, and your own categories with colours and auto-match sites.
Save every tab in a window at once, each into its own category.
Import your Chrome bookmarks into the library (a copy; originals are never changed), and export as a .html file Chrome can import, or a .json backup.
Optional: also add new saves to Chrome's own bookmarks, in an ElevenTabs folder with one subfolder per category.
Redesigned popup with Tabs and Saved tabs, tile actions and an at-a-glance search of what you saved. Saved pages also appear on the Welcome back page.
No new permissions: Saved lives in this browser profile only. Optional shortcut: assign a key to 'Save this page' at chrome://extensions/shortcuts.

title: ElevenTabs: Welcome back, themes and a new name
notes: New name: Tab Butler is now ElevenTabs, by YourElevens.
Welcome back page: pick up exactly where you left off, with a greeting, search, a daily recap, streaks and quick links. Opens when Chrome starts; switch it off any time. Shortcut ⌥⇧W.
Theme engine: 9 theme packs (Eleven Gold, Midnight, Aurora, Sunset, Forest, Graphite, Paper, Rosé, Sky), Auto mode that changes with the time of day, and your own custom accent colour.
Version number shown in the popup, dashboard and Welcome back page, plus this What's new page after every update.
Memory freed by sleeping tabs is now counted.

title: Premium redesign and work-safe security
notes: Gold-on-ink redesign with new icons, fonts and light/dark themes.
History and bookmarks became optional permissions, asked only when used.
No network access at all (strict security policy); private sites list; Erase data button.

title: First release (as Tab Butler)
notes: Auto tab groups, sleeping tabs, duplicate closer, sessions, bookmark tidy-up, history clean-up and a browsing dashboard.
